zh.summary: Palma.ai 为企业提供面向 MCP 工具与 Skill 的统一治理层，让员工在任意 AI 助手中使用经身份、策略与审计约束的智能体能力。
zh.judgment: 最关键的商业判断是：企业采用智能体的瓶颈正从模型能力转向权限、审批与可审计性，Palma 押注治理层会成为跨助手的独立基础设施，而非被单一模型厂商内置吞并。
zh.replaces: 替代各团队自行搭建的 MCP 网关、分散的 API 密钥与权限配置、人工审批邮件以及事后拼凑的日志审计流程。
zh.segment: 企业级 AI 智能体治理与 MCP 网关
zh.product: Palma 的核心产品是一个位于每个智能体与每个工具之间的策略层：通过单一连接器把 MCP 服务器和 Skill 按身份提供商分组下发到 Claude、ChatGPT、Copilot、Cursor 等客户端。它声称能检查工具调用的实际参数、对高风险动作暂停并要求具名审批人、对敏感字段做脱敏，并生成可用自有密钥离线验证的防篡改审计记录。平台还提供跨 Microsoft、Google、AWS 等注册表的统一目录，以及按智能体、团队和业务单元统计的用量与成本视图。以上均为公司披露，尚未经第三方验证。
zh.customer: 使用者是企业内被授予智能体权限的业务人员与工程团队，付费者更可能是 IT、安全和平台工程部门，因为官网明确以让 IT 敢于批准智能体做真实工作为卖点。痛点频率取决于企业智能体调用量：权限与密钥管理是持续性的日常负担，而审批与审计在合规审查、事故复盘和月末结算等节点集中爆发。目前没有公开客户名单或行业分布，无法判断其客户是大型受监管企业还是中型科技公司。
zh.workflow: 典型流程是：管理员通过 Entra 或 Okta 的 IdP 组把连接器分配给员工，员工在已使用的助手中直接获得其被授权的 MCP 工具与版本化 Skill，无需逐人安装或在本机保存凭证。当智能体发起工具调用时，Palma 读取请求参数并匹配策略，低风险调用放行并记录，高风险调用转给具名审批人，敏感数据在离开企业环境前被脱敏。最终每次调用都归因到人、智能体和应用，连同参数、结果、耗时与成本写入审计流并推送至既有 SIEM。
zh.business_model: 官网未披露定价、计费单位或合同结构，因此无法判断是按席位、按调用量还是按部署实例收费。可推断的部署模式包括 VPC、本地部署乃至完全气隙环境，并可选由 Palma 托管；这类交付通常意味着较重的实施与运维投入，单位经济可能偏向高 ACV 的企业合同而非自助订阅，但这是推断而非披露。缺少定价页是本次检索的主要缺口之一。
zh.traction: 可确认的采用信号有限：D11Z 与 Plug and Play 的投资人证言称其既是投资方也是客户，并称自己实际运行该产品；官网展示了若干策略、调用量与成本的界面示意。这些属于公司披露与投资人背书，不构成收入、客户留存或付费规模的证据。没有公开案例研究、客户数量、ARR 或续约数据，traction 判断应保持保守。
zh.moat: 相对通用模型厂商，Palma 的差异在于跨助手的中立性与企业内既有身份体系的深度绑定：规则写在治理层，换助手不必重配。相对自建网关，其壁垒取决于审计可离线验证、策略读取调用参数、以及 Skill 版本化分发这些工程细节能否稳定兑现。真正的护城河条件是成为企业采购中的默认治理标准并积累策略库与集成广度；若模型厂商把同等治理能力免费内置，或 MCP 标准本身吸收这些功能，中立层的价值会被压缩。
zh.funding_read: 本轮为 pre-seed，金额与原币由确定性层给出，投资方包括 Scale Now Ventures、D11Z Ventures、Deel Ventures 与 Plug and Play Ventures；名单不等于领投，资金用途未披露。该阶段说明产品已从概念走到可演示的企业部署形态，并获得至少一家投资机构的内部使用背书，但距离验证付费需求仍有距离。下一里程碑应是公开可核验的付费客户案例、定价结构以及安全合规认证。
zh.risks: 第一，若企业客户要求 SOC 2、ISO 27001 等认证或漫长安全审查，而 Palma 无法快速提供，销售周期会被拉长至超出 pre-seed 资金承受范围。第二，若模型厂商或 MCP 生态原生提供权限与审计能力，Palma 的中间层可能被视为可省略的附加成本。第三，气隙与本地部署虽迎合大客户，却可能造成实施成本高、复制性差，使收入增长依赖重人力交付。第四，策略误判导致合法调用被阻断或敏感数据未被拦截，都会直接摧毁信任。
zh.takeaway: 可借鉴的做法是把治理当作产品而非附属功能：用身份提供商组做权限分发、把策略绑定到调用参数而非仅绑定身份、并让审计记录可被客户用自己的密钥独立验证。另一个可学之处是把 Skill 定义为版本化、扫描后分发的企业流程资产，从而把最佳员工的操作方式产品化。
zh.watch_next: 下一步应观察：是否公开定价页与计费单位；是否出现具名付费客户案例及其部署形态；是否获得安全合规认证；以及策略执行与审计验证是否有第三方或客户公开验证。这些指标比融资额更能说明治理层是否真的被企业采购。

en.summary: Palma.ai offers enterprises a central governance layer for MCP tools and Skills, letting employees use identity-, policy- and audit-constrained agent capabilities inside whichever AI assistant they already open.
en.judgment: The key commercial bet is that the enterprise bottleneck for agents is shifting from model capability to permissions, approvals and auditability, and that this governance layer will persist as neutral infrastructure across assistants rather than being absorbed by a single model vendor.
en.replaces: It substitutes for per-team MCP gateways, scattered API keys and permission configs, manual approval emails, and logs stitched together after the fact for audits.
en.segment: Enterprise AI agent governance and MCP gateway
en.product: Palma positions a policy layer between every agent and every tool: one connector delivers MCP servers and Skills, assigned by identity-provider group, into Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor and other clients. It claims to inspect the actual arguments of a tool call, pause high-risk actions for a named approver, redact sensitive fields, and produce a tamper-evident audit record verifiable offline with the customer's own key. It also offers a unified catalog across Microsoft, Google and AWS registries plus usage and cost views by agent, team and business unit. All of this is company-reported and not independently verified.
en.customer: Users are business and engineering staff granted agent access; the payer is more likely IT, security or platform engineering, since the site explicitly sells letting IT say yes to agents doing real work. Pain frequency scales with call volume: credential and permission management is a daily burden, while approvals and audits spike around compliance reviews, incident postmortems and month-end close. No public customer list or industry mix is available, so it is unclear whether buyers are large regulated enterprises or mid-sized tech companies.
en.workflow: An admin assigns connectors through Entra or Okta IdP groups; an employee then receives entitled MCP tools and versioned Skills directly in the assistant they already use, with no per-user install or credentials on a laptop. When an agent issues a tool call, Palma reads the request arguments against policy, releases and records low-risk calls, routes high-risk ones to a named approver, and redacts sensitive data before it leaves the enterprise environment. Each call is attributed to the person, agent and application, with arguments, result, duration and cost streamed to the existing SIEM.
en.business_model: The site discloses no pricing, billing unit or contract structure, so it is impossible to tell whether Palma charges per seat, per call or per deployment. The disclosed deployment options include VPC, on-premises and fully air-gapped environments, optionally hosted by Palma; such delivery usually implies heavier implementation and operations effort and an enterprise-contract economics profile rather than self-serve subscription, but that is inference, not disclosure. The missing pricing page is a principal research gap.
en.traction: Confirmed adoption signals are limited: investor testimonials from D11Z and Plug and Play say they are both investors and customers and actually run the product, and the site shows interface mockups of policies, call volumes and costs. These are company-reported and investor-endorsed, not evidence of revenue, retention or paid scale. With no public case studies, customer counts, ARR or renewal data, traction should be judged conservatively.
en.moat: Versus general model vendors, Palma's differentiation is cross-assistant neutrality and deep binding to the enterprise's existing identity system: rules live in the governance layer, so swapping assistants does not require reconfiguration. Versus self-built gateways, the moat depends on whether engineering details such as offline-verifiable audit, argument-level policy and versioned Skill distribution hold up in practice. The real moat condition is becoming the default governance standard in enterprise procurement and accumulating policy libraries and integration breadth; if model vendors bundle equivalent governance for free, or the MCP standard absorbs these functions, the neutral layer's value compresses.
en.funding_read: This is a pre-seed round; amount and native currency are rendered by the deterministic layer, with investors including Scale Now Ventures, D11Z Ventures, Deel Ventures and Plug and Play Ventures. The list is not a lead designation, and use of funds is undisclosed. The stage suggests the product has moved from concept to a demonstrable enterprise deployment form and has at least one investor using it internally, but paid demand remains unproven. The next milestone should be publicly verifiable paying-customer cases, a pricing structure and security compliance certifications.
en.risks: First, if enterprise buyers demand SOC 2, ISO 27001 or lengthy security reviews that Palma cannot supply quickly, sales cycles may stretch beyond pre-seed runway. Second, if model vendors or the MCP ecosystem natively provide permissions and audit, the middle layer may be treated as an optional cost. Third, air-gapped and on-prem delivery, while attractive to large customers, may create high implementation cost and poor replicability, making revenue dependent on heavy human delivery. Fourth, policy misjudgment that blocks legitimate calls or fails to catch sensitive data would directly destroy trust.
en.takeaway: A transferable practice is to treat governance as the product rather than an add-on: distribute permissions via identity-provider groups, bind policy to call arguments rather than identity alone, and let customers verify audit records independently with their own keys. Another lesson is defining Skills as versioned, scanned enterprise process assets, turning a best operator's method into a productized capability.
en.watch_next: Watch for a public pricing page and billing unit; named paying-customer cases and their deployment form; security compliance certifications; and third-party or customer-verified evidence that policy enforcement and audit verification work as claimed. These indicators say more about whether the governance layer is actually purchased than the funding amount does.

Common Questions Quick answers about Palma.ai's enterprise MCP platform What is Palma.ai in one sentence? Palma.ai is the enterprise governance layer for MCP — it gives every person and agent a single governed connector carrying the tools and Skills they're entitled to, enforces policies on the actual arguments of a call, pauses high-risk actions for approval, and records everything in a tamper-evident audit trail. What does MCP governance mean? Deciding which person may use which tool, with which arguments, with whose approval — and being able to prove it afterwards. MCP itself covers how a client authenticates to a server and how a tool is described and called; it does not decide which person may use which tool, hold a risky call for a human, or keep the record an auditor asks for. Palma adds that layer: one governed connector per person, assigned by identity-provider group, carrying the tools and Skills they are entitled to into whichever assistant they already use. Does my team have to set up MCP servers themselves? No. Connectors are assigned by IdP group through Entra or Okta, so a joiner gets theirs on day one and a leaver loses it the moment the group changes. Every MCP server your team approves arrives through that same connector — no per-user install, no config files, no credentials sitting on a laptop. What's a Skill, and why does it matter? A tool is a verb — "send an email". A Skill is the playbook that tells an agent when and how to use the verbs it already has: how your team actually closes the books, runs an incident review, or qualifies a lead. Skills are versioned, scanned before they're served, and scoped like any other piece of enterprise software — so your best operator's process reaches everyone else's agent. Does it work with the AI clients we already use? Yes — everything is served over MCP, so the same connector, Skills and policies follow the person into whichever assistant they open, whether that's Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Cursor or something else. Switching tools doesn't mean re-approving, re-installing or re-auditing anything. How do we prove what an agent actually did? Every tool call is attributed to the person it was done for, the agent that did it, and the application it ran in — with the arguments, result, duration and cost. The audit trail is tamper-evident and verifiable offline with your own key, so your auditor doesn't have to take our word for it, and it streams to the SIEM you already run. How is Palma.ai deployed — SaaS, on-prem, VPC? Palma.ai is designed for enterprise environments: typically VPC or on-prem, including fully air-gapped, depending on your regulatory and security needs. The MCP layer and governance plane run on your infrastructure, so sensitive business data doesn't have to move into multi-tenant SaaS. We can also host it for you if you prefer.
